# Disagreement Log — 2 Maccabees Chapter 5

**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Agents:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Total Disagreements:** 20

---

## Disagreement 001 — v. 1: "second invasion"

- **EMET:** "made his second invasion of Egypt"
- **LOGOS:** "undertook his second campaign against Egypt"
- **PNEUMA:** "launched his second campaign against Egypt"
- **Note:** "Invasion" (EMET) is more dramatic; "campaign" (LOGOS/PNEUMA) is the standard military term. SOPHIA uses "campaign."

## Disagreement 002 — v. 2: Vision description — opening

- **EMET:** "there appeared in the air horsemen charging in golden gear"
- **LOGOS:** "there appeared in the air riders on horseback in golden armor"
- **PNEUMA:** "cavalry riding in gold armor"
- **Note:** EMET adds "charging" not in the Greek at this point; LOGOS is more literal. SOPHIA follows LOGOS.

## Disagreement 003 — v. 3: "forests of spears"

- **EMET:** "forests of spears"
- **LOGOS:** "formations of spears"
- **PNEUMA:** "spear-lines advancing"
- **Note:** Greek *lochismoi doraton* — formations/groupings of spears. "Forests of spears" (EMET) is a common poetic rendering but not in the Greek. SOPHIA uses "formations of spears."

## Disagreement 004 — v. 5: Jason's attack

- **EMET:** "Jason took no fewer than a thousand men and made a sudden attack upon the city"
- **LOGOS:** "Taking no fewer than a thousand men, Jason made a surprise attack on the city"
- **PNEUMA:** "Jason seized the moment — he gathered over a thousand men and launched a sudden assault"
- **Note:** PNEUMA says "over a thousand" where the Greek specifies "not fewer than." EMET and LOGOS are accurate. SOPHIA follows LOGOS.

## Disagreement 005 — v. 6: Reflexive tragedy

- **EMET:** "success against one's own kinsmen is the greatest of misfortunes"
- **LOGOS:** "success against one's own kin is the worst kind of failure"
- **PNEUMA:** "when you triumph over your own countrymen, there is no victory — only disaster"
- **Note:** Three very different renderings of the same Greek maxim. PNEUMA most paraphrastic. LOGOS inverts the idea ("success = worst failure") elegantly. SOPHIA: "success against one's own kinsmen is the worst of failures."

## Disagreement 006 — v. 8: Jason's end — description of his crimes

- **EMET:** "hated as a rebel against the laws and abhorred as an executioner of his country"
- **LOGOS:** "hated as a transgressor of the laws and abhorred as the butcher of his country"
- **PNEUMA:** "the man who had betrayed his country's laws and slaughtered his own people"
- **Note:** "Executioner" vs. "butcher" for Greek *miarios* — defiled/abominable. LOGOS's "butcher" is vivid and accurate. SOPHIA uses "butcher."

## Disagreement 007 — v. 9: Lacedaemonian kinship

- **EMET:** "in hope of finding protection there on account of their kinship"
- **LOGOS:** "in hope of finding protection there because of a supposed kinship"
- **PNEUMA:** "the Spartans, claiming kinship with the Jews, might offer him refuge"
- **Note:** LOGOS inserts "supposed" — an editorial judgment that the kinship claim was dubious. The Greek has simply *kata suggenian*. SOPHIA follows EMET's more neutral rendering.

## Disagreement 008 — v. 10: Jason's burial

- **EMET:** "he had no funeral of any kind and no place in the sepulcher of his fathers"
- **LOGOS:** "he had no funeral of any kind and no burial place in the tombs of his ancestors"
- **PNEUMA:** "no funeral, no place in his ancestors' tomb"
- **Note:** EMET uses "sepulcher" (archaic); LOGOS "tombs" (plural). Greek *en taphō patroōn* — in the burial place of the fathers. SOPHIA uses "tombs of his ancestors."

## Disagreement 009 — v. 11: Antiochus's reaction

- **EMET:** "raging in his mind he set out from Egypt"
- **LOGOS:** "raging in spirit, he departed from Egypt"
- **PNEUMA:** "Furious, he marched out of Egypt"
- **Note:** Greek *pikrainomenos* — embittered/enraged. "Raging in his mind" (EMET) is odd; "raging in spirit" (LOGOS) more natural. SOPHIA uses "raging in spirit."

## Disagreement 010 — v. 11: Taking the city

- **EMET:** "took the city by storm"
- **LOGOS:** "took the city by force of arms"
- **PNEUMA:** "fell upon Jerusalem with the full force of his army"
- **Note:** Greek *eipen tēn polin* — took the city. EMET's "by storm" is idiomatic. LOGOS's "by force of arms" is more literal. SOPHIA uses "took the city by force."

## Disagreement 011 — v. 13: Massacre description

- **EMET:** "a wiping out of women and children, a slaughter of virgins and infants"
- **LOGOS:** "a destruction of women, children, virgins, and infants"
- **PNEUMA:** "Women and children were slaughtered. Virgins and infants were put to the sword"
- **Note:** PNEUMA breaks into active voice with direct address. EMET and LOGOS retain the noun-heavy Greek list structure. SOPHIA follows LOGOS's list structure.

## Disagreement 012 — v. 14: Casualty numbers

- **EMET:** "eighty thousand were destroyed, forty thousand in hand-to-hand combat"
- **LOGOS:** "eighty thousand perished — forty thousand killed in hand-to-hand fighting"
- **PNEUMA:** "eighty thousand people were killed — forty thousand in direct combat"
- **Note:** All three agree on the numbers. Minor stylistic differences. SOPHIA follows LOGOS.

## Disagreement 013 — v. 15: Temple entry

- **EMET:** "he presumed to enter the most holy temple in all the world"
- **LOGOS:** "he had the audacity to enter the most holy temple in all the world"
- **PNEUMA:** "He had the gall to enter the most holy temple on earth"
- **Note:** "Presumed" (EMET) is more neutral; "audacity" (LOGOS) and "gall" (PNEUMA) are stronger. Greek *etolmēsen* — dared. SOPHIA uses "had the audacity."

## Disagreement 014 — v. 17: Theological commentary — Antiochus's error

- **EMET:** "not perceiving that the LORD was angered for a little while on account of the sins of those who dwelt in the city"
- **LOGOS:** "not perceiving that the LORD had been provoked to anger for a short time because of the sins of those who dwelt in the city"
- **PNEUMA:** "He could not see what was really happening: that the LORD had allowed this, for a brief time, as a judgment on the sins of the people"
- **Note:** PNEUMA substitutes "allowed" for "angered/provoked to anger" — a significant theological difference. The Greek *di' hamartias tōn enoikountōn ōrgizeto ho despotēs* — the Sovereign was angry because of the sins of the inhabitants. SOPHIA follows LOGOS.

## Disagreement 015 — v. 19: Key theological statement

- **EMET:** "God did not choose the nation for the sake of the holy place, but the place for the sake of the nation"
- **LOGOS:** "God did not choose the nation for the sake of the holy place; he chose the place for the sake of the nation"
- **PNEUMA:** "God had not chosen the nation for the sake of the holy place. He had chosen the holy place for the sake of the nation"
- **Note:** All three are accurate; the reversal structure differs. PNEUMA uses two sentences. LOGOS introduces with "he chose" in the second clause. SOPHIA follows LOGOS.

## Disagreement 016 — v. 20: Temple's shared fate

- **EMET:** "afterward participated in its good fortunes"
- **LOGOS:** "afterward shared in its recovery"
- **PNEUMA:** "would share in its restoration"
- **Note:** Greek *tēs euemerēsias metaschon* — sharing in the prosperity/good fortune. LOGOS's "recovery" is interpretive. EMET's "good fortunes" is more literal. SOPHIA uses "participated in its good fortune."

## Disagreement 017 — v. 21: Antiochus's arrogance

- **EMET:** "thinking in his arrogance that he could make the land navigable and the sea passable on foot"
- **LOGOS:** "thinking in his arrogance that he could make the land navigable and the sea passable on foot"
- **PNEUMA:** "In his delusion, he actually thought himself powerful enough to make the sea walkable and the land navigable"
- **Note:** PNEUMA reverses the order (sea/land) and uses "delusion" instead of "arrogance." EMET and LOGOS agree. SOPHIA follows EMET/LOGOS.

## Disagreement 018 — v. 24: Apollonius's orders

- **EMET:** "commanding him to slay all the grown men and to sell the women and the young"
- **LOGOS:** "with orders to kill all the grown men and to sell the women and the youth"
- **PNEUMA:** "His orders: kill every adult male; sell the women and the young"
- **Note:** PNEUMA uses imperative fragments for a military command register. LOGOS's "youth" vs. EMET's "young." SOPHIA follows LOGOS.

## Disagreement 019 — v. 25: Sabbath ambush

- **EMET:** "pretended to be peaceably disposed and waited until the holy sabbath day"
- **LOGOS:** "made a show of peaceful intentions and waited until the holy sabbath day"
- **PNEUMA:** "played the peacemaker. He waited. When the sabbath came"
- **Note:** PNEUMA breaks into fragments for dramatic pacing. LOGOS's "made a show" is vivid and accurate. SOPHIA uses LOGOS.

## Disagreement 020 — v. 27: Judas's withdrawal

- **EMET:** "lived like the wild animals in the mountains along with his companions"
- **LOGOS:** "lived in the mountains in the manner of wild animals with his companions"
- **PNEUMA:** "They lived in the mountains like wild animals"
- **Note:** All three convey the same. LOGOS preserves "in the manner of" — slightly more formal than "like." SOPHIA follows LOGOS.
